result: All three current audit findings confirmed and fixed locally. Existing uncommitted work preserved.

findings.change: Separate live-public browser routing; shared CONNECT-only proxy rejects private/reserved/transition IPs and mixed DNS answers, pins a validated IP, and refuses all plain HTTP including certificate-looking paths.
Closed shadow controls and isolated draft/validated selector state. Genuine input updates the draft; saving revalidates that state without rereading the control.
Recorded policy and behavior use the same parsed options, including clicks implied by --popups-only. Plain HTTP is actually denied.

visualReview.result: Picker text and controls visible, aligned and within viewport; focus and preview state readable

validation.beforeAfter: Original picker persisted the substituted selector. Original launcher reached the owned loopback canary. Both regression cases pass after the fixes.

limitations: Firefox automation rejects extension-popup navigation before the first assertion. Saved pre-change launcher and picker reproduce the same failure; one retry also timed out during session.subscribe. Firefox runtime behavior remains unverified.
No live target sites were opened. DNS and tunnel policy were tested with synthetic answers and owned loopback transports, not production DNS or public services.
The conservative live proxy can reject special-purpose public services or sites requiring HTTP certificate-chain retrieval. It is not an operating-system sandbox.
The extension in a personal browser profile was not reloaded; reload the unpacked extension to activate the picker change.
